say: Eyegore doesn't argue with a problem. He ends it, and then the problem is a report.
I've seen him once, on the Heng road. The crows moved to the other side.
The Captain-General has never once been late. Think about what that means.
Nobles whisper that the Empire has one answer to every question, and it's armoured.
He was bred in the South and sent north to be useful. He is very useful.
Pay your taxes. Eyegore is what the taxes are for.
Their general is a Hiveless drone. Even the Hive wouldn't take him back, and the Empire made him a god of war.
I heard Eyegore walked through a shield wall like it was wet paper. I heard it from a man missing the shield.
Put the Cities out of mind, they say. Put Eyegore out of mind. One of those is easier.
Nobody I know has fought him twice. That tells you something about the first time.
Hiveless and southern-born and the Empire's finest edge. I would be curious about him, if I were less afraid.
The Empire's soldier is no-hive. A lost one, bent into serving them. The hive doesn't take him back.
We hear of the lost one called Eyegore. He walks like a drone and kills like none of us. We don't say his name twice.
Hiveless, and the Empire calls him captain. The hive would have used him better.
No-hive, and still he obeys. We obey because we're one. What does he obey?
Stay off the roads where the Empire's samurai ride. The lost one rides behind them.
There's a drone in the Empire they send when everything else has failed. That's all I know.
Stay off the roads where samurai ride in fives.
People say Eyegore never sleeps. Probably untrue. Probably he just doesn't need to.
Wronged the Cities badly enough, and the last thing you see is a Captain-General.
Everyone I have met who talks about Eyegore is lighter in the pocket and longer in the silence.
A soldier drone with an empire's boot behind him. Don't be what he's aimed at.
Eyegore is dead. Say it again and tell me it still sounds like a thing that can happen.
The Captain-General fell and the barracks went so quiet I could hear a ledger turning.
Somebody has to tell Lord Tengu's court. I'm glad it won't be me.
They carried him in on a gate. A samurai wept and tried to pass it off as dust.
The Empire leaned on him for a lifetime. Now we all lean on nothing.
Whatever was coming for the next trouble, it just lost its edge.
Eyegore, the Empire's mad dog, in the dirt. The Flame does not call it a mercy aloud, but it is one.
The Cities lost their great blade. Say what you like of the heretic who did it, the roads are safer.
Hiveless to the end. Even in dying he belonged to no one. A pity, and a mercy.
Everyone on this side of the border is breathing lighter. Everyone on that side has gone to count their soldiers.
The Empire's captain is down. Pray the next is not cleverer.
The lost one called Eyegore is dead. He belonged to no hive. We didn't know him.
A no-hive drone fell in the Empire's service. The hive doesn't mourn the lost.
We hear the Empire's soldier is gone. We feel nothing. We aren't sure why we say it twice.
Hiveless to the end. Even the dead need a hive.
Someone broke what the Empire made. The hive watches the one who did.
Eyegore, the Empire's mad dog, in the dirt. I'd buy the one who did it a drink and then keep a wall between us.
The Cities lost their great blade. I won't call it a mercy aloud, but it's one.
Someone put Eyegore down. Whoever it was, the Cities will be watching the roads for them.
He was a slave too, in his way, bent to the Empire's will. I won't mourn him. I won't cheer either.
One less leash in the Empire's hand. Spring will hear of it tonight.
A flatskin put Eyegore down. Remarkable. The Shek will remember the name and watch the road.
The Empire's mad dog is dead. A Shek would have done it with more ceremony, but I will not complain.
Hiveless in life, nameless in death. Even a warrior deserves a name on the stone.
The Cities lost their great blade. Their soldiers will want revenge. Honour won't be theirs.
I'd have met him sword to sword. Whoever did it took that from me, and I'm almost grateful.
I heard Eyegore fell. Not to a battle. To a cut. A single cut, with the whole Empire watching.
They say the Captain-General died at the hands of a hundred. Or one.
The Empire is bleeding somewhere south. A great soldier gone, and every thief in Heng is grinning.
Somebody finished Eyegore. Don't ask me who. Nobody who knows is saying.
A wall fell in the Cities. Only a man, they tell me, but a wall.
Whoever it was, I hope they enjoy a short and well-defended life.
Eyegore in a cage. I have to say it twice to make my mouth believe it.
The Captain-General is a prisoner. There's a price on his return, and a bigger one on those who took him.
I keep waiting for a samurai squad to ride out and settle it. Perhaps they're waiting too.
They didn't kill him. They kept him. That's worse, in the way it leaves a door open.
Taken alive, gods help us. Whoever has Eyegore has the Empire's undivided attention.
Eyegore is in chains. The Flame has a great many uses for a soldier like him, and for the one who holds the key.
A cage for the Cities' best blade. I wonder who feeds him, and what he thinks about while he eats.
Eyegore alive and held. The Empire will tear the plains up looking, so do not be the plains.
Better a living Eyegore in a cell than a dead one in a legend. Dead ones do not bargain.
A Hiveless drone in a cell. Even a heretic's cage is kinder than the Empire's leash.
The lost one is held in a cage. We feel the empty place where a hive would be.
No-hive, and in a cage. The hive wouldn't have kept him so. The hive would have used him.
The one the Empire made is held. We watch the one who holds him.
We hear the Empire searches. The hive doesn't search.
Eyegore held, and Grey would want to talk to him.
A cage for the Empire's best blade. A soldier is a slave too, with a different collar.
If anyone can make a lost one remember being a drone, it's us.
Better him in a cell than on the roads. Whoever holds him, do not let him loose.
Eyegore is caged. A warrior should die on the field, not wait in a cell. Even for him, a cruelty.
A flatskin holds the Empire's blade. The Shek will watch to see how long he keeps it.
Hiveless and held. The Stone Golem would not weep for him.
The Empire will tear the plains up looking. Let them. The Shek have watched armies pass before.
I heard they took the Captain-General alive. Alive! Nobody takes anyone like that alive.
Eyegore is somebody's prisoner. That sentence has never been true before this season.
There's a drone in a cell somewhere who used to be the worst thing in the Empire. Now he's a rumour.
Do you know what the Empire pays for a general back? I don't either, but I hear it's more than the whole bar.
They didn't kill the Empire's blade, they borrowed him.
You're the one who ended Eyegore. The Empire has a long memory and a short list of names, and you're on it.
There's a ledger for what you owe now. Eyegore alone is more than your whole life.
That's the face. That's the face that did it.
You cost us our Captain-General. I'll cost you the rest.
Murderer of the army's right hand. Run, if you must. It will be a short run.
You hold Eyegore. Give him back, or watch how much heavier the Empire can be.
You kidnapped the Captain-General. Nobody is that brave.
Every blade in the Cities is looking for you. We only hope to find you first.
Release him, and I may see to it that your death is a quick one.
Hiveless one is gone. No hive weeps.
This one was Southern once. Not any more. Not ever. It's better this way.
The Faraway empire lost a drone. We don't count it a loss.
Fallen: a soldier with no queen. The queen would say nothing.
You. The one they say put Eyegore down. Don't stand near me, the Empire watches me too.
A soldier drone, a captain-general, and you. The world is changing. I don't like how it sounds.
Careful. Anyone who killed Eyegore has people hunting them who also watch from windows.
I won't ask. I'll say only: good, and also, please move along.
There's a sort of silence that follows you. It's the silence of a road with fewer soldiers on it.
Eyegore ended. That chain won't close on us this season. You have our thanks, and our caution.
Many of us marched into his spears in the old days. You marched out.
A great weight left the world when he fell. I won't say the name again, to save us the shiver.
We have stories of the Captain-General. Now we have a better one: how he ended.
I heard you're holding Eyegore. Don't tell me where. Don't tell me anything.
A cage with that inside it must be heavy to keep. I almost envy you the weight.
You took the Captain-General alive and walk about with that face? Brave.
I'd feed him well, if it were me. A well-fed monster is only half a monster.
My Captain-General is dead and you stand before me. Convenient that I can't deduct it from your fee.
Eyegore was my insurance. You have made me uninsured. We shall negotiate that.
Nobody breathes in this hall without wondering if they're next. You did that.
I paid for that soldier's every breath. The price you owe isn't small.
You hold Eyegore alive. Good. A man like that is more use turned than broken.
Don't harm him more than the work needs. A soldier is a slave too, with a different collar.
I'd speak to him, if you'll allow it. Chains teach nothing, but sometimes a listener does.
He was a drone before he was a weapon. I want to find the drone again.
Longen counts the cats and the cats are afraid to be counted wrong.
The throne room in Trader's Edge has a view of everything that's for sale.
I've never seen him, but I have paid him. Every merchant has. That's its own kind of seeing.
He doesn't tax, he assesses. There's a difference, and he will explain it very slowly.
There's a story the Guild has no door he can't open. Another says he has no door he can't close.
The nobles swear to him before they swear to anyone. Tengu holds the sword.
Trader's Edge buys and sells people the way other towns sell bread. Longen owns the shop, the bread, and the bakers.
When a chain breaks in the Cities, I think somewhere Longen frowns and writes down the cost.
Tinfist rails against him and Longen yawns. The yawn is more frightening than the rails.
Everyone owes the Guild something. Longen only collects.
He's smart. That's what you must remember. A fool on a throne can be forgotten, he can't.
I won't speak of him within sight of a Guild shop. Even walls there carry weight.
Trader's Edge buys and sells people the way other towns sell bread. Longen owns the shop, the bread, and the bakers.
Every collar I have cut was paid for with Guild coin.
When a chain breaks in the Cities, I think somewhere Longen frowns and writes down the cost.
Tinfist rails against him and Longen yawns. The yawn is more frightening than the rails.
He's smart. That's what we must remember. A fool on a throne can be forgotten, he can't.
Trader's Edge buys and sells people the way other towns sell bread. Longen owns the shop, the bread, and the bakers.
Every collar I have ever worn was warmed by a Guild coin.
When a chain breaks in the Cities, I think somewhere Longen frowns and writes down the cost.
Tinfist rails against him and Longen yawns. The yawn is more frightening than the rails.
I won't speak of him within sight of a Guild shop. Even walls there carry weight.
Whoever holds the roads holds the trade, and the Guild holds the roads. Whoever holds the Guild is called Longen.
You can buy anything from his people. Anything. Ask a slave if you doubt it.
A trader from Heng told me the king of commerce never leaves his chair.
There are men who run empires and men who own them. I am told Longen is the second kind.
He would sell a flood to a fish, and the fish would sign.
Longen is dead. The market in Trader's Edge stopped for an hour. First time in my life.
They're already arguing over his chair. Nobody is brave enough to sit in it.
Without him, who signs the manifests? Who buys the debts? We're a ship without a keel.
I lit a lamp for the old accountant and then checked my own books for threats.
The man who owned the slave trade of an empire went down like anyone else. I keep turning it over.
Prices are already moving. A kingmaker dies, and the cats wake up trembling.
The Guild lost its head. The Free Traders will pretend to mourn and be selling in his markets by month's end.
Longen dead? Then the roads are a little less owned. Some of us call that a good day.
I have no love for traders, yet even I notice the quiet where Longen used to hum.
Somebody took the largest slaver in the Empire off the board. Whoever it was did us a favour we can't repay.
It will take years for the Guild to bury him properly and about a week for it to bury the story.
The king of the markets was killed. I heard it from three merchants. Each said a different year.
Longen is dead, they say. Can a thing like that die? I always thought him furniture.
Somebody cut the throat of the Empire's purse. Prices in the south have been wild since.
A slaver of that size, and nobody mourns him loudly. That is its own sort of epitaph.
A man in a throne room died, and half the continent breathed out.
They took Longen. Alive. The Guild is offering a ransom nobody will pay in full.
Silence in the Edge. His own guards are staring at their boots.
An empire's worth of debts, and the man holding the ledger is in a cell. Imagine the creditors.
I don't know what's worse for us. If he returns, or if he doesn't.
Longen in a cage. I thought only slaves could be told what to eat.
The Guild's master is held. For once, someone else is setting a price.
Taken alive, I heard. A hostage worth a thousand slaves. What would you ask for?
Longen caged. The jokes write themselves, and every one of them costs a coin to tell.
I hope he is learning the weight of the iron he sold.
They kept him breathing. Someone is very patient, or very greedy.
A man who can buy anything finally finds something that isn't for sale: his own door.
You're the one that killed our master. The Guild shall find its own accounting for that.
Longen's blood on your hands, and you walk our road.
Whatever you carry, you carry over his grave. The Guild collects on every debt.
I swore my oath to him before I swore any other. Have your death, stranger, and make it quick.
He wasn't kind. He wasn't just. He was mine. I'll take you for it.
Where's the Guildmaster? Tell me, or I'll carve it out of you.
You hold Longen? The ransom was always going to be your life. You didn't read the terms.
He fixed prices for kings. What do you imagine he has done to yours?
Release him, and I'll let you hope for a quick end.
You killed Longen. I don't need telling. The way people step aside makes it plain.
You do realise half the roads in the Empire were his, do you not? And the other half were also his.
Strange. I expected a monster. You look quite ordinary.
Hush. If a Guild man hears I spoke to you, I lose a customer and a hand.
Longen is gone. Listen to the roads. Quiet.
Thousands wore his collars. Few will ever tell you his name without spitting after.
You cut the largest chain in the world. We'll carry the thanks of it as far as our own can go.
You hold the Guildmaster. Don't let him speak too much. He sells with a mouth.
Alive, then. Good. Let him count the days the way his slaves did.
If the iron fits, use it. If it doesn't, find iron that does.
Longen dead. Tinfist will hear of it. He may not say anything. He may not need to.
You've done what we spoke of for years. We shall not make a song of it, but we'll remember.
I have been taught the dead can't be wronged further. I'm still glad it's him who's dead.
A slaver of that size, finished. Do you feel lighter? Some do.
The Guildmaster is dead. That leaves me with the same prisoners and fewer people to blame.
Fascinating. You walk in here on the heels of Longen's death. I am almost impressed.
Don't look so pleased. The one who replaces him will have the same appetite, with fewer manners.
Longen gone, and Tengu's Vault still has a lock. The world is stubborn, is it not?
The Old Prison has a big something living in it. Big, and bored, and very touchy about names.
Don't call him a gorilla. Don't call him anything. Don't go near the Old Prison, in fact.
I saw a man thrown from the Old Prison wall. He landed far past where a man ought to land.
They tell me Gorrillo cries when he loses at games. I tell them I do not plan to be there to see.
The Gorrillo Bandits are the only ones who can say his name without wincing. They wince later.
Something in the Old Prison eats and eats and still looks bored. Somebody must feed it.
BOSS BIG. BOSS STRONG. BOSS PUNCH DOOR. DOOR GONE. YOU NEXT.
Don't CALL BOSS APE. BOSS HEAR. BOSS NOT HAPPY.
OLD PRISON IS OURS. BIG ONE LIVES THERE. YOU NOT GO IN.
WE FEED BOSS. BOSS KEEP WALLS. TINY GO AWAY.
BOSS CRY WHEN LOSE AT GAMES. Don't LAUGH. WE ALL TRY NOT TO.
SIXTY THOUSAND CATS ON BOSS. NOBODY COLLECT. NOBODY COME BACK.
The big one is down. I keep waiting for a roar. Nothing. It's worse than the roar.
Big as a wall and slow as one. Half the bandits out here liked him anyway.
The Old Prison is empty now. Nobody wants to be the first one to walk in and look.
Who smashes the doors now? Who carries the heavy things? The Forbidden Zone will miss him.
Sixty thousand cats on him and it took one stranger. The Old Prison won't feel the same.
The thing in the Old Prison is dead. I can hear the roads being less loud.
You hear about Gorrillo? Some drifter did him in. I'd love to see that fight, from very, very far.
A giant, they said, with a taste for locked doors. Now he's a story.
Whoever beat that great ape deserves a medal. Or a long rest. Or a priest.
Everyone in the badlands slept easier last night, and a few of them cried.
They put him in a cage. A cage! Can you imagine what holds that?
Gorrillo held. I'd pay to watch that hold, from very far away.
He isn't killed. He's simply unhappy, and unhappy is the more dangerous.
The bandits are leaderless and nervous. They keep looking at the horizon for a roar.
The big one is somebody's now. May whoever has him love him better than the Old Prison did.
YOU SMASH BIG ONE! ME SMASH TINY YOU!
BIG ONE GONE. TINY DID IT. ME SQUISH TINY.
HUR HUR. NO MORE BIG ONE. NOW ME SMASH.
ME NOT LIKE TINY NOW. ME HUG TINY. TOO HARD.
BIG ONE DOWN. ME WAIT FOR ROAR. NO ROAR. IS WORSE.
WHO SMASH DOORS NOW? WHO CARRY HEAVY THINGS? NOT ME. YOU DO IT, TINY.
GORRILLO DIE BORED. NOW YOU DIE BUSY.
WHERE BIG ONE? GIVE BACK OR ME BREAK TINY HEAD!
BIG ONE IN BOX. BIG ONE HATE BOX. YOU HATE MORE.
YOU TAKE BIG ONE. ME SMASH TINY. PLEASE RUN. ME LIKE CHASE.
BOSS HATE BOX. BOSS BREAK BOX. THEN BOSS BREAK YOU.
OLD PRISON QUIET WITHOUT BOSS. TOO QUIET. ME NOT LIKE.
I hear you dropped the great ape of the Old Prison. How big were the bones? Big, I bet.
You're the one who went into the Old Prison and walked out. Don't stop here, you'll frighten the horses.
No one comes out of there. You did.
Sit, drink, and say nothing about the ape. Please.
Go to Spring and speak to Grey. He asks who your enemy is.
He turns people away. Not cruelly. He asks what you would do if the collar were on your own neck.
I was a slave. Grey didn't ask what I had done. He asked what I'd do next. That was all.
They say he never raises his voice. They also say few raise theirs at him.
Tinfist is the face of the thing.
He guides the new ones. If the ones he guides survive, the movement survives.
Grey is dead. Who will ask the new ones where they stand? Who will hold the door?
He asked every one of us one question. Now there's no one to ask it.
Spring is grey today. I don't mean the sky. I don't mean the stone.
Tinfist said a few words over him. Nobody remembers them, only the quiet.
We'll do what he would have done. We won't do it well.
One of the troublemakers is dead. They'll make a martyr of him, but a martyr is cheaper than a living nuisance.
Grey, the Anti-Slaver at Spring, is dead. One less voice telling slaves they have a choice.
The Anti-Slavers lost their recruiter. That's a quiet kind of victory, and I'll take it.
One death in Spring, and a great deal of quiet. Strange how those go together.
Tell your friends: the road to Spring just got a little longer.
Grey is dead. One less voice telling the cargo it has a choice.
The Anti-Slaver at Spring has fallen. Runaways will lose heart, and the roads get easier for us.
Their recruiter is dead. Their camp is a headless dog, for now.
Grey is gone. I won't pretend to be sorry. Business will be good this season.
Grey in chains. The irony would be funny if it weren't so exact.
They took the man who frees slaves. Whoever did it has made a lot of enemies in Spring.
He won't break. Men like that don't.
The recruiters have gone to ground. The camp at Spring is waiting, and counting hours.
Grey in a cage. Spring won't sit still for that.
Grey in a cage. Now we see how he likes being on the wrong side of the bars.
The one who guides runaways has been taken. Prices are about to improve.
Grey in chains. Somebody should send Tinfist a collar, as a gift.
The Anti-Slavers lost their spine. Expect them to come looking, and expect them to be sloppy.
The Anti-Slaver leader caged. Someone has done what the Cities could not.
Grey in chains. The recruiters will be scrambling, and the camp at Spring will be furious.
They took the man who frees slaves. There will be a price for that, and not only in cats.
A famous troublemaker in a cell. Trade sleeps easier tonight, and wakes uneasy.
You killed Grey. You're a dead thing walking, and I'll see it done.
Grey believed in second chances. I'm not nearly as kind.
He asked every stranger the same question. You answered it with a blade.
Spring won't forget. Neither will I.
You hold Grey. We're coming. All of us.
Take the collar off him, friend. It's an easy thing, and it's the last easy thing you'll be asked.
You're a slaver. I didn't think I'd say that of anyone who walked here.
You stand with us, and Grey is gone. We shall do it together, then.
He wouldn't want revenge. He would want the door left open for the next one.
Come sit with us. There's no one to ask the question, so ask yourself.
You're the one who ended the Anti-Slaver at Spring. They'll want to know your name, stranger.
Killing the gentle ones. That is a certain kind of courage, or the other kind.
Half the roads now have Anti-Slaver eyes on you. I wouldn't go to Stobe's Gamble.
You've been busy with the tyrants. A small joy. Don't let it become a taste.
Spring has heard of what you do. Tinfist has said nothing.
Prove you're the enemy of our enemy, and the door opens. It seems you proved it more than once.
Be careful whom you serve in turning. Some fall because they enjoyed it.
There was a warrior once named Suchon. We don't say it. The one who walks out there's called by something else.
He lost, they say. That's all the Kingdom says. A warrior who loses should die.
Go east of Last Stand and the Berserkers sing for him. It's a song with no words.
I have seen him once. He did not fight. He looked at the horizon as if it owed him an answer.
Some say he wants to be struck down. Some say the blade will not finish him. Neither helps.
A Shek without a Kingdom is a ghost. The name came easily to the people who gave it.
There's an exile out east they call the Ghost. Nobody calls him it to his face.
A Shek exile who can't die properly. Sounds like a story.
East of Last Stand there's a camp where nobody sleeps well. You'll know the horns.
The Ghost hasn't lost a duel in years. He's looking for a loss that will take.
They say he's sad. They say being sad hasn't made him slower.
Ghost is gone. The one thing none of us could be, he was. Now he's that thing for good.
He wanted it. We know he wanted it. We still do not forgive the one who gave it.
The camp is loud and nobody is speaking. There's a space where he sat.
We never believed the Kingdom would take him back. We never believed anything could stop him.
Sing for him. Sing badly. He liked it that way.
The exile is dead. Peace to him, whatever peace means to a Shek.
Suchon died, finally. Let the name be said once, quietly, and put down.
It was a death the Kingdom wouldn't give him. An outsider did, I hear. I find that strangely fitting.
The Berserkers are leaderless. A bad season for the east is coming.
He walked the world for years looking for an end. Somebody just found it for him.
They took the Ghost alive. Of all the things he feared, I think that was the one.
Locked. A warrior who sought death, held out of its reach.
The Shek police will want him. Not for what he did.
The Berserkers wait. Waiting is a slow poison to them.
If you can chain a ghost, you can chain anything. I'd be very careful of whoever did.
You killed the Ghost. We'll honour him by killing you. Slowly.
He said no one was worth fighting any more. You were. Now you'll be again.
The one who ended Suchon. We have your scent. Hide if you like. We love hide and seek.
Blood for the Ghost. Blood, stranger.
You hold our Ghost. Open the door or lose the hands that closed it.
A warrior chained is a sin. A cage for him is worse.
Fight us, flatskin. Or are you only brave with the weak and the sad?
You're the one who ended the exile. The Kingdom didn't ask this of you. But we won't weep.
A flatskin slew the Ghost. Strange. Honourable, in a way. I do not know what to feel.
Walk well, outlander. The Shek do not forget that someone took a burden from us.
Suchon is gone. The name has weight.
The Princes come when the fog thickens. Close the shutters and keep the lamps low.
A Prince can stand in a ring of spears and look bored. Then the Fogmen come, and no one is bored.
We hear them at night. Not screaming. Humming. It's the humming that kills the mind.
The Shinobi guards hold the gate. Don't ask what they hold it against. Ask who sleeps.
My brother went to the fog for treasure. A Prince had him by sundown. I think of it as a thing that happened to the weather.
A Prince's head sells for a good price. Almost nobody ever sells one.
The Fog Islands. Don't go. Whatever they pay you, don't go.
They were Hivers once, I am told. Now they are something else, and it sits in a Prince's head.
A Prince eats the ones the Fogmen drag in. Alive. That is the thing I cannot stop knowing.
A Prince of the fog. I saw a drawing of one in a bar. I left the bar.
There's a parasite, so I hear. That's the polite word for what the fog does.
Fogmen carry the prey to the Prince. The Prince decides which part first.
A Prince is dead. The fog sounded different last night. Quieter. Not gone.
Some stranger killed one of them. Well. Let us hope the others didn't notice.
I want to see the head. I don't want to be in the room with the head.
Another Prince will come. They always do. But for tonight the walls feel thicker.
Whoever it was, they went into the fog and came out. Sit, let me buy you something.
I heard somebody killed one of the fog princes. Or maybe it killed them and walked away.
A prince of the Deadhive, dead. The Islands will be hungry, they say, to replace him.
The head fetches six thousand cats. That's a lot of cats to hold in a hand that smells of fog.
Kill one Prince and I expect another takes the place. In the fog I hope that's untrue.
Stranger, whoever did it: do not go back. The fog keeps a ledger.
They took one alive. In a cage. I keep imagining the sound it makes.
A Prince, held. Whatever holds it, I hope it's stronger than the thing in its head.
People want to see it. People are fools. People will be eaten.
Keep it alive, keep it fed, keep it far. That's the Mongrel prayer now.
The fog prince is held. The hive felt the song go thin. We do not understand it. We worry.
A prince in a cage. We hum for him. He does not hum back.
Don't hurt the held one. Don't hurt us.
The fog prince is far and afraid. We feel that much.
You smell of fog. Keep your distance. The fog follows some people home.
Killed a Prince, I heard. We'll see if the fog agrees you won.
Mongrel can give you a drink, a bed, and a long look.
You went in and came out. Do you hear it still? That humming? I do.
There's a throne in the domes. A very old one sits in it. It has been sitting a very long time.
Cat-Lon founded what the Empire was. Then he held it too tightly. I haven't recorded the result.
He ordered a whole people once. Now he orders an empty dome, and the dome doesn't answer.
He isn't mad, precisely. He's correct about many things, for many reasons, all of them wrong.
He speaks of treason. He speaks of thralls. He speaks of the first mistake. It's always the same speech.
I don't go near the domes. I measure the distance.

Mad Cat-Lon. The name comes up whenever someone sells a map of the Ashlands. The maps are always wrong.

Word is, he isn't mad, only correct for reasons that are all wrong.

There's a skeleton in the Ashlands who used to rule an empire. He rules a dome now.
The Second Empire fell and one still sits in his throne. I hear he talks to the walls.
Mad Cat-Lon. Say it softly. The name has a way of arriving in a room.
People say he thralled his own people to save them. They say he's still saving them.
An empire of metal, held together by one lonely mind. I would not stand in that mind's way.
Dome after dome in the Ashlands, and a ruler in the last one. I won't visit. Please don't ask.
The old ruler has ended. I'm not sure what I feel. I have no entry for this.
The throne is empty. It was the only thing that gave the domes meaning, and now there's no meaning.
He built something and then he broke it. He's dead now.
I recall his voice. I recall the first time he spoke to me. I recall not being able to disagree.
The CPU left the dome in a human's pocket. That's a ridiculous end for a founder.

Cat-Lon scrapped. The domes are open for business, and every Tech Hunter in the Ashlands knows it.
He ruled an empire and ended in a dome. A fitting end, if anyone is keeping records.
The throne is empty. Whoever did it walked out again. I'd like to buy that person a drink.
Mad Cat-Lon is dead. I didn't know that could happen. I thought he was a weather.
Somebody went into the Ashlands domes and came out. That alone should be a legend.
The skeleton king is no more. His empire was already no more. Now the ruin is formally complete.
A founder of the old world, scrapped in his own dome. History has an odd taste for irony.
Somebody will call it a victory. Somebody calls everything a victory. This time I almost agree.
They took Cat-Lon alive. What do you do with such a thing in a cage? Who dares hold the key?
Taken. A ruler without a dome. I wonder if he still gives orders to the walls.
The oldest mind in the Ashlands, a prisoner. The jailer must hear things at night.
I wouldn't ask what he says. I'd only shut the door more tightly.
Cat-Lon is held. I don't know what holds him.
The oldest mind in the Ashlands is in a cell. I wouldn't guard it.
A ruler without a dome. He may still be giving orders. The walls are listening, or aren't.

You're the one who removed Cat-Lon. I'll say nothing. I'll think a great deal.

states: Queen of the South killed by player
